title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: new strict URI validation in AL Http Client
summary: Business Central v28 introduces stricter URI validation in AL HttpClient to prevent Server-Side Request Forgery attacks by blocking HTTP requests to internal and non-routable addresses by default. Cloud environments enforce this without bypass options, while on-premises deployments offer configuration settings to whitelist trusted internal addresses when necessary.
key_points: Strict URI validation blocks HTTP requests to localhost, private IP ranges, link-local addresses, and other non-public network addresses
SSRF protection is mandatory in cloud/SaaS environments with no bypass options available
On-premises deployments can use NavHttpClientAntiSSRFEnabled and NavHttpClientAntiSSRFAllowedAddresses settings to manage restrictions
Security enhancement is backported to versions 26.x and 27.x for consistent protection across supported versions
Extensions relying on internal integrations may need refactoring to use public APIs, Logic Apps, or other managed integration solutions

quotes.text: Starting with Business Central v28, outgoing HTTP calls made through the AL HttpClient are subject to hardened URI validation.
quotes.why_it_matters: This is the core change developers need to understand and plan for when upgrading their extensions

quotes.text: For organizations using Business Central online, there is no way to bypass this security restriction. This is intentional and non-negotiable.
quotes.why_it_matters: Cloud customers must understand they cannot disable the protection, making extension refactoring mandatory for internal integrations
